name: Acidity
description: The bright, tangy sensation on the sides of your tongue — not sourness from a flaw, but a lively quality often compared to citrus or apple. Lighter roasts and washed coffees tend to have more of it.

name: Body
description: How heavy or light the coffee feels in your mouth, from tea-like and thin to syrupy and thick. Brew method affects this a lot — French press and espresso tend toward fuller body than pour-over.

name: Sweetness
description: A perceived sugariness that comes from how well the coffee was grown, processed, and roasted — not added sugar. Described with references like honey, caramel, or brown sugar.

name: Aftertaste (finish)
description: What lingers on your palate after swallowing. A short finish fades quickly; a long finish continues to evolve for a while after each sip.

name: Balance
description: How well acidity, sweetness, and body work together, with no single quality overpowering the others.
